title: Hundreds of beach trees felled in Cox's Bazar for a tourism carnival
excerpt: The Forest Department says it gave no permission to cut the casuarina trees, which protect the coast from storms. Green groups want an inquiry.
content:
Several hundred casuarina (jhau) trees, some decades old, were allegedly cut down on the beach in Cox's Bazar to make room for a 90-day tourism event called the Cox Carnival, The Financial Express reported on 18 November. The trees form a natural protective barrier along the coastal belt and reduce wind speed.

Mizanur Rahman, range officer of the Sadar Range in the Cox's Bazar South Forest Division, told the paper that no permission had been given to fell the trees. Fazlul Kader Chowdhury, convener of the Cox's Bazar chapter of the environmental group Dharitri Rokkhae Amra (DHORA), called the felling unacceptable and suggested the event use an open trade fair ground instead. Environmentalists and local people have called for an investigation, legal action against those responsible and replanting. The paper also spoke to Md Mahmudur Rahman Sayem, assistant commissioner at the district Tourism Cell.

Why it matters

Coastal green belts cut storm surge and erosion, and they take years to grow back. Cox's Bazar is exposed to cyclones and tidal surges. Environmental and disaster risk reduction NGOs working on the coast have pushed for these belts to be protected and extended.

What to watch

Whether the Forest Department files a case, whether the district administration orders replanting, and whether the carnival goes ahead on the same site.
